fields.meta_title: Cancellation Survey Builder With Reason Routing | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a cancellation survey from a prompt: a reason list, a pause offer, delivery-zone alerts, feature counts, and reason trends. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Cancellation Survey That Acts on Every Reason
fields.hero_description: Build a cancellation survey that asks why customers leave, sends each reason to its owner, and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Cancellation Survey Built by Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the cancellation survey, the logic for each reason, and the table of answers, and changes any of it by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A reason list answered in one tap

Describe the reasons customers give when they leave, and Emergent builds a question with one tap per reason, an Other option, and an optional comment box under the list.
fields.feature_2:
A next screen that depends on the reason

Each answer can open its own next screen: a pause offer after Too expensive, a feature question after Missing a feature. Describe each branch and Emergent writes the logic.
fields.feature_3:
Plan and signup date beside each answer

The app can pull each customer's plan and signup date from your billing tool through its API, so every reason sits in your own database next to the account that gave it.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when one reason piles up

Set a threshold, like 10 late delivery reasons in one zone in a month, and the app sends an email or Slack alert to the person who owns that fix, with the answers attached.
fields.feature_5:
Every cancellation gets its survey

Emergent sets no response caps on surveys. The survey runs on every cancellation, in a quiet month or a month when 3,000 customers leave, and each answer lands in one table.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, then your repository

Host the survey on a custom domain, which Emergent includes and which uses credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository to read and edit line by line.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Cancellation Surveys, Four Next Steps
fields.tab_content_1:
A pause offer for anyone who says Too expensive

Wordsail, a language-learning app, asks every subscriber who cancels for one reason and an optional comment. Picking Too expensive opens an offer to pause the plan for 2 months, and No thanks finishes the cancellation. In September, 61 subscribers picked that reason and 18 of them took the pause.
fields.tab_content_2:
Operations hears when a zone hits 10 late deliveries

Pantry Post saves each meal kit cancellation reason with the customer's delivery zone. When one zone collects 10 or more Late delivery reasons in a month, the app emails its answers to Ruthanne Pickett, the operations lead. In October, East Valley had 23 among 47 cancellations; no other zone had more than 4.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each Monday, product sees which features were missing

Trackwell sells scheduling software to field-service companies. A canceling customer who picks Missing a feature is asked which one, and every Monday the app sends the product manager, Cosima Brandauer, a count by feature. Since July, 40 customers named one: 14 wanted route optimization and 11 offline mode.
fields.tab_content_4:
Quayside adds a class after 19 schedule cancellations

Kinloch Fitness asks each member who cancels to pick a reason, and tallies the reasons by studio and month. At the Quayside studio, Class times don't fit grew from 4 cancellations in July to 9 in August and 19 of 42 in September. The studio manager added a 6:15 am weekday class the next week.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Cancellation Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a cancellation survey that customers can skip in one tap and that tells each team which reason to fix.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep the reason list short and rotate it
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about one thing per option
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add a comment box at first
fields.howto_step_1_des: Before writing a question, list what the answers could change, such as a price test or the next feature on the roadmap. Tie each reason in your list to one of them. Put that list in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the survey around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Offer 5 or 6 reasons plus Other, worded the way customers talk. Pew Research Center notes that people answering self-administered surveys tend to choose items at the top of the list. Rotate the order for each customer and keep Other last.
fields.howto_step_3_des: An option like Too expensive and hard to use asks two things at once. Questions that ask respondents to evaluate more than one concept are what Pew Research Center calls double-barreled. Split it into two options. Each tap then counts toward a single reason.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Leave a free-text box open under the reasons for the first month. Pew Research Center says researchers will sometimes run a pilot with open-ended questions to discover which answers are most common. Rewrite the list around the words customers typed.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put a Skip link on every screen of the survey, and make it complete the cancellation in one tap. Test that path before any other. A customer who skips should land exactly where one who answered does: canceled, with a confirmation on screen.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Compare reasons by plan and tenure
fields.howto_step_6_des: Save the plan and signup date with each answer. Then compare Too expensive on the monthly plan against the annual one, and reasons from customers in their first 90 days against those from customers who stayed for years.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Pretest it, then read it monthly
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before launch, have 3 coworkers cancel a test account and note where they pause. Pretesting is, in Pew Research Center's words, an essential step in the questionnaire design process. After launch, read the reasons by segment each month and act on the one that grew.

faq_plan.a: A cancellation survey is a short set of questions a customer answers while ending a subscription, starting with why they are leaving. Memberful's help center describes its own as a survey that collects feedback from members when they cancel a subscription. The answers show which reasons repeat and who should act on each one.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a cancellation survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI survey builder: the reasons to list and what each one opens next. Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it from that prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes any part of it. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What cancellation survey questions should I ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with one: What is the main reason you're canceling? Then ask one follow-up tied to the answer, such as Which feature were you missing? after Missing a feature. End with an optional box for anything else. Write each option in words a customer would use, and leave out internal labels like Churn risk.

faq_plan.q: What do cancellation survey examples look like for different businesses?
faq_plan.a: A good one keeps the reason question and changes the follow-up to fit the business. A meal kit service could ask which delivery went wrong after Late delivery, and scheduling software which feature was missing. To test one fix with past customers, such as whether an earlier class would bring them back, a single question in a yes no questions survey gives a clean count.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a cancellation survey have?
faq_plan.a: Two or three: the reason, one follow-up that depends on it, and an optional comment. Each extra screen sits between the customer and the cancellation they came to make. Emergent puts no cap on survey responses, and the short version can run on every cancellation.

faq_plan.q: Should a cancellation survey offer a discount or a pause?
faq_plan.a: Only after a reason the offer answers. A pause fits Too expensive or Taking a break; it does nothing for Missing a feature. Show one offer, once, and record whether it was taken next to the reason. Emergent builds that branch from one sentence in your prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a cancellation survey use a light, friendly tone?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in the wording around the questions, like a short thank-you line or a goodbye on the confirmation screen. Keep the reason options plain and free of jokes, and every answer counts cleanly. Jokes fit better in funny survey questions people answer for fun than on a screen someone sees on the way out.

faq_plan.q: How do you analyze cancellation survey results?
faq_plan.a: Count each reason by month, then split the counts by plan or by signup month. A reason that grows in one segment points to one fix, like a delivery zone or a missing feature. Emergent can build the dashboard that charts those counts, and every answer stays in a database you own for any other query.

faq_plan.q: When should a cancellation survey appear?
faq_plan.a: Right after the customer clicks cancel, before the cancellation is final. FastSpring's cancel survey, for one, appears when a customer initiates a subscription cancellation. Keep the reason question on that first screen as a single tap, with nothing to type.

faq_plan.q: Should a cancellation survey use multiple choice or open text?
faq_plan.a: Both, in that order. A multiple-choice reason gives you a count to chart, the way poll questions do: one tap, one tally. An optional text box after it catches the detail a list misses, like which competitor or which feature. Keep that box after the list, never in place of it.

plan.angle: The top 10 is SaaS blog guides (Usersnap, Paddle, Baremetrics, Chargebee, Responsly, involve.me, Stay.ai) that list reasons and sample questions, plus two template galleries (Jotform, Wufoo). They stop at the list of reasons. This page shows four cancellation surveys built from a prompt, each ending in an action: a pause offer after Too expensive, a delivery zone with 10 or more late-delivery reasons going to the operations lead, missing features counted for the product manager each Monday, and a studio adding a class after one reason climbs. The FAQ answers what a builder asks: which questions, how many, offers, tone, timing, analysis and question format.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Cancellation Survey That Acts on Every Reason'; hero 'Build a cancellation survey that asks why customers leave, sends each reason to its owner, and saves it to a database you own.' covers the whole job; how-to description one sentence with the primary.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is SaaS guides listing questions and reasons plus Jotform/Wufoo templates; the page gives questions (FAQ 3 'What is the main reason you're canceling?'), examples (four tabs, FAQ 4), question count, offers, timing, analysis and a 7-step how-to.

specificity.evidence: Subscription vocabulary: 'a pause offer after Too expensive', 'compare Too expensive on the monthly plan against the annual one', 'customers in their first 90 days', 'Let Skip finish the cancellation'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Wordsail, a language-learning app, asks every subscriber who cancels...', 'Trackwell sells scheduling software to field-service companies.', 'Before writing a question, list what the answers could change...'

craft.evidence: Sentences mostly carry one idea ('Test that path before any other.'); one ', so' ending in feature_3 and a 34-word sentence in feature_4 (QC P2, noted).

voice.evidence: Concrete and unglamorous: 'I only practice on weekends now.', 'a 6:15 am weekday class', 'have 3 coworkers cancel a test account and note where they pause'. Two FAQ answers bent around link anchors are noted.

truth.evidence: Emergent sentences map to prompt-build, database-owned, api-connect, alerts, no-caps, custom-domain, code-export, free-start. Third-party facts match quoted spans: Memberful ('collects feedback from members when they cancel a subscription'), FastSpring ('appears when a customer initiates a subscription cancellation'), Pew (primacy in self-administered lists, double-barreled, open-ended pilot, pretesting 'an essential step'). Numbers agree: 18 of 61; East Valley 23 of 47 with others at 4, 3, 1; 14+11+9+6=40; 4, 9, 19 of 42.

distinct.evidence: Own angle (each reason ends in an action: pause offer, zone alert, Monday feature count, new class); tab H3s use no sibling primary; sibling primaries only as FAQ link anchors (yes no questions survey, funny survey questions, poll questions).

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic builder questions, answer-first ('Two or three: the reason, one follow-up...', 'Only after a reason the offer answers.', 'Both, in that order.'); hub link in item 2; 3 sibling links; secondaries 'cancellation survey questions' and 'cancellation survey examples' in questions 3 and 4; PAA gate 10 pass, 0 reject, 0 flag.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: Wordsail 'Pause for 2 months', 'No thanks finishes the cancellation', '18 took the pause of 61 who chose Too expensive'; Pantry Post table East Valley 47/23 'Emailed' with other zones at 4, 3, 1 and card 'To Ruthanne Pickett'; Trackwell '40 customers named one since July', 14 route optimization, 11 offline mode, card 'To Cosima Brandauer', 'Sent every Monday'; Quayside 4, 9, 19 of 42 and '6:15 am weekday class added'.
